newsitem.title: USA: Dlr ends mostly firm in US, stg surges post-budget.
newsitem.headline: Dlr ends mostly firm in US, stg surges post-budget.

text.p: *Dlr ends mostly firm in US after setting third successive 40-mo peak vs mark of 1.7550. Dlr/yen creeps up after hit overseas by Thai baht flotation. Fed keeps rates unchanged, sparks fleeting dollar losses. Stg ends at highs, moves above 2.94 marks, nears $1.68 after UK finmin Brown offers less-than-austere budget, keeps UK rate hike hopes alive.
The dollar pushed to another 40-month peak against the mark on Wednesday, but fell sharply against a surging pound after Britain's Labor government unveiled its first budget.
Sterling initially stumbled lower when UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown began his budget speech by saying that he shared British industry's concern about the strength of the pound.
But as the details of the budget emerged the pound began a sharp rise, climbing almost three cents against the dollar and a whopping five pfennigs from its lows versus the mark.
Dealers said the budget had not contained the austere fiscal measures necessary to curb strong consumer-led growth in the UK, leaving the door open for a near-term hike in UK interest rates.

"Brown's initial remarks took sterling down to the lows but the rest of his comments were well received and we saw heavy buying of sterling," said Cynthia Johnson, managing director of foreign exchange at CIBC Wood Gundy.
"I think people perceived the budget as leaving the door open for higher interest rates."

The pound surged to a high of $1.6785 before settling at $1.6765/75, well above Wednesday's opening rate of $1.6590/00. It also ended U.S. trade at a new five-year peak of 2.9430 marks, helping the dollar post gains against the mark as well.
Also supporting the dollar against the mark was a report showing that German industrial production had fallen by a surprising 0.2 percent in May.
The dollar closed at 1.7545/55 marks against 1.7506/10 at the open, after hitting a 40-month peak against the German currency of 1.7550 -- its third top in as many days.

"We're starting to touch on significant technical levels between 1.75 and 1.76 marks," said John Beerling, chief dealer at Norwest Bank. "Most people are looking for this to top out around here but if it continues higher it opens the door for 1.85, 1.90 and perhaps 2.00."

The dollar ended marginally higher against the yen, which attracted safe-haven buying interest during Asian trading hours after the Bank of Thailand announced it was dropping its pegged exchange rate system and letting its currency float freely.

As the U.S. session unfolded and the markets digested the news, the yen's strength faded somewhat. The dollar ended at 114.45/55 yen, up from 114.35/45 at the open, but off Tuesday's closing level of 114.90/95.
The British budget announcement and the news out of Thailand overshadowed the Federal Reserve's decision to hold interest rates steady at the conclusion of its two-day policy meeting on Wednesday.
The dollar fell slightly after the rate decision, briefly poking below 1.75 marks, but its losses proved fleeting. The markets had widely expected no rate change from the Fed.
In other trade on Wednesday, the dollar rose to 1.4710/20 Swiss francs from 1.4685/95 at the open. The dollar slipped to Canadian $1.3757/62 from C$1.3780/85.
And the Australian dollar ended at $0.7516/21 against $0.7532/37.
